summary: Klamath County, OR: 1930 tree cab and steel LS-40 tower, staffed into the 1950s, dismantled 1979; no dated source describes the site today; undated photo captions and a county list mention its remains.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with 7x7 cab (about 107 ft), built after a 1930 tree crow's nest cab
facts.status_note: Dismantled in 1979. An undated county list says the 1930 crow's nest tree has come down and is heavily decayed. Undated WillhiteWeb photo captions mention tower footings and a ground house foundation; no dated source describes current condition.
facts.agency: Klamath Indian Reservation (register); Oregon Department of Forestry from 1961 (WillhiteWeb)

visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb lists the hiking distance as drive-up. The register names the Klamath Indian Reservation as administrator. No source describes current access.

events.note: 107-foot steel Aermotor LS-40 tower erected in September and October by the Indian Service (one county list credits the Crater National Forest)
Register says a 110-foot steel tower and house replaced the tree in 1932; other sources date the steel tower to 1930

Marian Doty spent the summer as lookout

Mrs. Claude Parazoo had been lookout for the past eight years; electricity run up to the tower
Responsibility for maintenance and operation passed to the Oregon Department of Forestry
Two fires reported from this station

corrections.why: Sources from 1931 onward and the county list give about 107 feet (32.6 m). The register's 110 feet was the height ordered in 1930, not the height most sources describe for the standing tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates a 110-foot steel tower and house to 1932. The 1930 newspaper and survey items, WillhiteWeb and the county list date the 107-foot LS-40 tower to 1930. A 1940 survey note gives 105 feet. The story gives the 1930 date and 107 feet and notes the disagreement.
Two sources say the Indian Service built the steel tower. The county list says the Crater National Forest erected it with the Indian Agency. The story reports both.

The register names the Klamath Indian Reservation as administrator. WillhiteWeb says the Oregon Department of Forestry took over maintenance and operation in 1961, and a 1974 summary shows it under that department's control.
One 1941 item spells the lookout's name Yader and the parenthetical reads Yoder. The story uses Yoder.

notes_for_editor: Brief height 33.5 m (110 ft) is corrected to 32.6 m (107 ft); the register's 110 ft and 1932 date conflict with most other sources and both are in resolved_conflicts. Brief's Aermotor design is confirmed (LS-40). Brief's access 'permission' has no source support: sources name the reservation as administrator and WillhiteWeb lists drive-up, but none states a permit rule, so no access level is recorded. WillhiteWeb photo captions (tower footings, ground house foundation) have no image URLs captured, so no photo entries are added. Staffing as_of is the 1979 dismantling year.
